requirements: session.access scope=ubus object=file function=exec (uhttpd omits scope)
session.access scope=file object=canonicalized executable or cmdline function=exec
assumptions: Synthetic handler_effect transcribed from rpcd-mod-file rpc_file_exec; C, not ucode

uhttpd uh_ubus_allowed requires session.access scope=ubus object=file function=exec (uhttpd omits scope). rpcd-mod-file then requires session.access scope=file of the canonicalized executable or, on miss, of the cmdline. A ubus file.exec grant is not authorization to run an arbitrary command.

rpc_file_exec_run checks the executable file ACL first, then the cmdline. That is the reverse of cgi-io main_exec. Inventoried luci-ssl ACLs grant the bare /bin/umount and /sbin/block executables, so extra tokens match at the executable stage as intended_access for the mounts fixture, not authorization_violation and not a PoC.
This oracle does not fork execv or run the command body.
shellquote and basename are not sanitizers. rpc_canonicalize_path is a textual path normalizer, not a taint sanitizer.

These commands are not luci object methods. Do not invent a luci object grant. Callers at luci b2e0be4b use fs.exec → ubus file.exec. getBlockDevices / setBlockDetect popen/system of /sbin/block stay on the luci object grants.
rpc_file_exec_run returns PERMISSION_DENIED when both SID and env are present. Inventoried callers do not pass env.
The luci-mod-system-mounts fixture is already list read/write for luci.getBlockDevices / luci.setBlockDetect. This slice reuses that session; it does not invent a second mounts login.
evidence_refs: rpcd@d99f703e file.c rpc_file_exec_run executable then cmdline file ACL
unknowns: Live uhttpd, rpcd, and rpcd-mod-file were not executed; decisions are transcribed from pinned C and ACL JSON.
rpc_file_exec_lookup PATH search and live stat(2) are not modeled. This oracle treats only the inventoried absolute command paths as found.
execv of the command, helper-internal argv after the file ACL, and file.exec of commands other than inventoried /bin/umount and /sbin/block are not modeled.

cgi-io cgi-exec stays on policy:cgi-exec-v1 / cgi-exec-file-v1 / cgi-exec-status-v1. luci-mod-status iptables -Z / routes ip stay on policy:ubus-file-exec-v1. luci-mod-network-config ifup/ifdown/wifi stay on policy:ubus-file-exec-ifup-v1. luci-mod-status-processes /bin/kill stays on policy:ubus-file-exec-kill-v1. luci-mod-network diagnostics ping/traceroute use fs.exec_direct without a cgi-io grant on luci-mod-network-diagnostics, so they are not this slice. crontab.js fs.exec of cron reload has file.exec of the cmdline but ubus file.write not file.exec. luci-mod-system flash.js sysupgrade/firstboot stay unstaffed. Track A is unstaffed. dispatcher is not this slice.
rpc_file_access returns true when ubus_rpc_session is absent (local ubus callers). HTTP /ubus injects the parsed SID after uh_ubus_allowed; this oracle does not model the plugin skip as an allow.
